cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and the thinking has gone quiet on its own.
cells.act: go deeper into the shared thing than comfort allows
cells.ask: With a group you belong to, say the thing you usually keep at a safe distance — plainer than you'd normally put it — and stay there after you've said it.
cells.core:
Something you share with other people is getting ready to move, and you can feel it coming before anyone else does. A group, a family, a thing you do together is reaching the edge of how it has run, and the way through is the way it has gone before: one person says the true thing out loud, and the rest follow. That is not avoiding the moment. That is how the moment gets met.

So go deeper with them than you usually let yourself. Pick the shared thing where you are holding something back and say it plainly, the version you trimmed to keep it comfortable, then stay after you have said it. Not a speech and not a repair. What you have together is what carries the group past the old way, and you are the one who walks it there.
cells.sheetLine: You already belong, so say the truer thing.
cells.verb: resting the mind on purpose so it settles
cells.place: where you see how a thing works with the labels off

cells.tense: You are bracing for how this will go before it has started.
cells.act: keep the heading when it is contested
cells.ask: Pick out a direction you actually chose, and when someone next pushes you off it, stay on it once — no argument, just staying.
cells.core:
Your mind won't sit still. It keeps running the next conversation, the next objection, the next way this goes wrong, and that isn't rest, it's rehearsal. You read the room ahead of time and call it clarity. From outside it looks like you have decided how everything ends before anyone speaks. Underneath, you do see how things work, and that part is sound. The thinking has just stopped being restful and started being a defence.

So don't try to think less. Hold one thing instead. Take a direction you genuinely chose, not a preference, and the next time it is contested, stay on it once. Defend it without needing to win the argument. That is the mind coming back to its own balance: not emptier, steadier.

cells.tense: You stood at that door a while, and it is behind you now.
cells.act: let yourself be drawn before you choose
cells.ask: Notice what tugs at you — a room you keep almost entering, a person you keep almost calling — and go a little way toward it before deciding if it's right.
cells.core:
There is a quietness in you that isn't rest, it is distance, and you have stayed back from what used to move you until staying back became the habit. You can still tell how a thing works with the labels off. What has thinned is the pull, being drawn toward something before you have reasoned it out. You have been picking from a short catalogue instead of from want.

So follow the pull once, before you are sure. Something already tugs at you, a room, a person, a thing you keep meaning to do, and the move is not to decide whether it is right. It is to go a little way and see what it is up close. No plan and no verdict afterward. Forward, once, and let wanting have a vote.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped letting yourself want before you know.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you are already, quietly, writing in.
cells.act: leave the hollow ritual for the living one
cells.ask: Take one shared practice that has gone empty and skip it once — quietly — and spend that same time on something that still has life in it.
cells.core:
Something you share with people is being kept alive, and you are the one keeping it. The meeting that stopped mattering, the way the group still greets each other, the version of you who shows up because you did last time. Asked, you'd say you are just going along with it. You are not. You are the one holding it up, gently, by not letting it end.

So give the old shape a place to stop, literally. Not a declaration and not a conversation, just a day you mark for yourself when you skip the hollow thing once, and put that time into something with life in it. What the others feel as thinning becomes a thing you did, on a day you picked. Nobody needs it explained.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the old thing going without calling it yours.
